title: Earthwork volumes and the mass-haul diagram: cut, fill and balance

curves.label: Embankment section
curves.ask: How do you calculate the area of a road cross-section?

explain.say: A new road over rolling hills means digging through the high parts, called cuts, and building up the low parts, called embankments or fills. Moving millions of tonnes of earth is one of the biggest costs of the job. It starts with a cross-section. On the board, an embankment two metres high.

curves.label: Embankment section
curves.ask: How do you calculate the area of a road cross-section?

explain.say: Look at its shape: a flat top ten metres wide, with sides sloping two across for every one up. Its area is the top width plus the slope times the height, all times the height: ten plus four, times two, twenty eight square metres. Why are the sides sloped, not vertical?

curves.label: Embankment section
curves.ask: How do you calculate the area of a road cross-section?

explain.say: So the soil does not slump! Now volume. Take sections twenty metres apart, twenty and thirty square metres. Average the end areas and multiply by the gap: five hundred cubic metres. But dug soil is fluffy. A cubic metre from the ground fills about one point two five in a truck and squeezes to zero point nine once compacted.

draw.text: Prismoidal: L/6 (A₁ + 4A_m + A₂) gives 493 m³ when A_m = 24.5 m².

explain.say: Now the mass-haul diagram. Add up the volumes along the road, cut as plus, fill as minus. Look at the curve: it rises while the road is in cut and falls while it is in fill. The peak at four hundred metres is exactly where cutting ends and filling begins. What does a falling curve mean?

Filling! Where the curve returns to zero, at about seven hundred and sixty seven metres, everything dug so far has been placed: a balance point. Beyond it the road ends eight hundred cubic metres short, so soil must be brought in from a borrow pit. Excellent! Challenge: sections forty and sixty square metres, twenty five metres apart: what volume?

faq.q: How do you calculate the area of a road cross-section?
faq.a: For level ground, area equals the formation width plus the side slope ratio times the height, all times the height. A 10 metre top, 2 metres high with 2 to 1 slopes, gives 28 square metres.

faq.q: What is the average end area method?
faq.a: The volume between two cross-sections is the distance between them times the average of their areas. Twenty metres apart with 20 and 30 square metres gives 500 cubic metres.
asks: How do you calculate earthwork volume between cross-sections?

faq.a: A more exact volume: L over 6 times the first area plus 4 times the middle area plus the last area. It suits curved or changing sections.
A graph of cumulative earthwork volume along a route, cut positive and fill negative. Rising parts are cut, falling parts are fill, and where it crosses a horizontal line the cut and fill balance.
asks: How do you read a mass-haul diagram?

faq.a: Soil swells when dug, often by about 25 percent for common earth, and shrinks when compacted. Volumes are converted between bank, loose and compacted states for planning trucks and fill.

facts: On a mass-haul diagram, a rising curve means cut and a falling curve means fill.
The prismoidal formula gives exact volumes for solids whose cross-section area varies as a quadratic along their length.
